questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the FIFA World Cup 2026:
1. It was the first World Cup to be played with 48 teams.
2. The final was won by Argentina.
3. The final was played at the New York New Jersey Stadium (MetLife Stadium) in East Rutherford.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final on 19 July 2026. The tournament was jointly hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico, so the second statement reverses the result.
questions.h: 48 teams, three hosts, one winner: Spain.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026:
1. It was co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka.
2. India defeated New Zealand in the final at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad.
3. It was India's third T20 World Cup title, after 2007 and 2024.
4. Jasprit Bumrah was named Player of the Tournament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India won the final by 96 runs and Bumrah was Player of the Match, but Sanju Samson was named Player of the Tournament. The title came after the 2007 and 2024 wins.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup 2025:
1. India beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final.
2. The final was played at the DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai.
3. It was India's second Women's World Cup title, after 2005.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India won its first ODI World Cup title in 2025 and had lost the earlier finals in 2005 and 2017. Shafali Verma was Player of the Match in the final and Deepti Sharma Player of the Tournament.
questions.h: Third time lucky: lost finals in 2005 and 2017, won in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Commonwealth Games:
1. The Glasgow Games ended on 2 August 2026.
2. India finished fourth in the medal table at Glasgow 2026 with 39 medals.
3. India will host the centenary edition of the Games in 2030 at Ahmedabad.
4. India has previously hosted the Commonwealth Games in 1982.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India hosted the Games only once before, at New Delhi in 2010; the 1982 event in Delhi was the Asian Games. India won 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze at Glasgow, with fewer sports on the programme than Birmingham 2022.
questions.s: ETV Bharat, 3 Aug 2026; Free Press Journal, Aug 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 Asian Games:
1. They were held at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.
2. India finished fourth with 85 medals, including 21 gold.
3. India's medal tally was higher than its 107 medals at Hangzhou.
4. China topped the medal table with 169 gold medals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India's 85 medals fell short of the record 107 at Hangzhou 2022 (held in 2023), so the third statement is wrong. China led with 169 gold and 341 medals in all.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics:
1. The Games were hosted jointly by Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo in Italy.
2. Norway topped the medal table with 18 gold medals.
3. India won a medal in cross-country skiing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India sent two athletes, Arif Mohammad Khan (slalom) and Stanzin Lundup (cross-country skiing), and won no medal. Norway finished first, ahead of the United States and the Netherlands.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Men's FIH Hockey World Cup:
1. Germany won both the 2023 and 2026 editions.
2. The 2026 final was played between Germany and Argentina.
3. The 2026 edition was hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Germany beat Belgium on penalties at Bhubaneswar in 2023 and beat Spain 1-0 in the 2026 final, taking a fourth world title. Argentina finished third in 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ICC Champions Trophy 2025:
1. India beat New Zealand by four wickets in the final.
2. The final was played at the Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore.
3. India's matches in the tournament were played in Dubai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under the hybrid model agreed because India did not travel to Pakistan, the host, India played all its games, including the final, at Dubai. It was India's third title after 2002 (shared) and 2013.
questions.h: Hybrid model: Pakistan hosts, India plays in Dubai.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian chess:
1. Gukesh Dommaraju became the youngest World Chess Champion at the age of 18.
2. He won the 2024 title by defeating Ding Liren of China.
3. Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025 by beating Koneru Humpy in the final.
4. India won gold only in the Open section at the 2024 Chess Olympiad in Budapest.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India won gold in both the Open and Women's sections at Budapest in 2024. Gukesh won in Singapore in December 2024, and Divya's 2025 win at Batumi also earned her the Grandmaster title.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. India win the Women's Cricket World Cup
2. Gukesh becomes World Chess Champion
3. India win the ICC Champions Trophy
4. India win the Men's T20 World Cup 2026
questions.e: Gukesh won in December 2024, the Champions Trophy followed in March 2025, the Women's World Cup in November 2025 and the T20 World Cup in March 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Athlete : Result at Paris 2024 Olympics
1. Neeraj Chopra : Silver medal in javelin throw
2. Manu Bhaker : Bronze medal in women's 10 m air pistol
3. Lakshya Sen : Bronze medal in men's badminton singles
4. Vinesh Phogat : Silver medal in women's 50 kg wrestling
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Lakshya Sen finished fourth, and Vinesh Phogat was disqualified before the final for being overweight, so neither won a medal. India won six medals at Paris, one silver and five bronze.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics:
1. Cricket in the T20 format will be included.
2. The additional sports were approved at an IOC Session in Mumbai in October 2023.
3. Cricket was last played at the Olympics in 1948.
4. Squash is among the additional sports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The five added sports are baseball/softball, cricket, flag football, lacrosse and squash. Cricket was last played at the Olympics in 1900 in Paris, not 1948.
questions.h: Five new sports: Baseball/Softball, Cricket, Flag football, Lacrosse, Squash.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Sports Governance Act, 2025:
1. It received Presidential assent in August 2025.
2. It provides for a National Sports Board, a National Sports Tribunal and a National Sports Election Panel.
3. Recognised sports bodies are public authorities under the RTI Act for all their functions.
4. Appeals from the National Sports Tribunal lie to the Delhi High Court.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Recognised bodies are treated as public authorities under the RTI Act only for their statutory functions. Appeals from the Tribunal generally go to the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The first recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award (1991-92), now renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, was
questions.e: Anand received the first Khel Ratna in 1991-92. The award was renamed after hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand in 2021; Tendulkar, Paes and Bindra received it in later years.
questions.s: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about future FIFA World Cups:
1. The 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup will be hosted by Brazil.
2. The 2030 men's World Cup will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Italy.
3. The 2034 men's World Cup will be hosted by Saudi Arabia.
4. Some centenary matches of the 2030 World Cup will be played in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2030 tournament will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, so the second statement names the wrong third host. South American matches mark the centenary of the first World Cup, held in Uruguay in 1930.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India at the Paralympic Games:
1. India won 29 medals at Paris 2024, its best-ever tally.
2. India won 8 gold medals at Paris 2024.
3. India's previous best was 19 medals at Tokyo 2020.
4. India finished among the top five countries in the Paris 2024 medal table.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India won 7 gold, 9 silver and 13 bronze at Paris, finishing 18th. The Tokyo 2020 total of 19 medals was the earlier record.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India has won eight Olympic gold medals in men's hockey.
Statement-II: India's last Olympic gold in hockey came at Moscow in 1980.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: India won golds in 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964 and 1980. The second statement is also correct but does not explain the count of eight.
questions.h: Six in a row until 1956, then 1964, then 1980.

questions.q: In 2021, the IOC added a word to the Olympic motto 'Faster, Higher, Stronger'. The word added is
questions.e: The motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' became 'Citius, Altius, Fortius - Communiter', that is, 'Faster, Higher, Stronger - Together', to stress solidarity. The other words are tempting but not part of the motto.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.
2. Milkha Singh won India's first individual Commonwealth Games gold in 1958.
3. The Fit India Movement was launched on 15 August 2019.
4. India won the Thomas Cup in 2022 by defeating Malaysia in the final.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Fit India Movement was launched on 29 August 2019, National Sports Day and Major Dhyan Chand's birth anniversary. India's 2022 Thomas Cup win in Bangkok came against Indonesia.
questions.s: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports; BWF

questions.q: The five interlocking rings of the Olympic flag symbolise
o: the union of the five inhabited continents
the five oceans of the world
the five original sports of the Games
the five founding nations of the modern Games
questions.e: The rings stand for the union of the five continents and the meeting of athletes worldwide at the Games. They were designed by Pierre de Coubertin in 1913.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Stadium) with List-II (City):
A. Narendra Modi Stadium
B. Kalinga Stadium
C. Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium
D. Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium
1. Rourkela
2. Ahmedabad
3. New Delhi
4. Bhubaneswar
questions.e: The Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad hosted the T20 World Cup 2026 final, Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar and Birsa Munda Stadium in Rourkela hosted the 2023 Hockey World Cup, and Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi staged the 2010 Commonwealth Games opening.
questions.s: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports; ICC; FIH

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Royal Challengers Bengaluru won the IPL 2026 final against Gujarat Titans at Ahmedabad.
2. IPL 2026 was Royal Challengers Bengaluru's maiden IPL title.
3. South Africa beat Australia in the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord's.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RCB retained the title in 2026 after winning their maiden title in 2025, so the second statement is incorrect. South Africa's win at Lord's gave them their first ICC trophy since 1998.

questions.q: India's highest medal tally at a single Olympic Games, seven medals, came at
questions.e: Tokyo 2020 brought one gold (Neeraj Chopra), two silver and four bronze. London 2012 and Paris 2024 each gave six medals and Rio 2016 only two.

questions.q:
Match List-I (National Sports Award) with List-II (Year instituted):
A. Arjuna Award
B. Dronacharya Award
C. Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna
D. Dhyan Chand Award
1. 1985
2. 2002
3. 1961
4. 1991-92
questions.e: The Arjuna Award came first, in 1961, then the Dronacharya Award for coaches in 1985, the Khel Ratna in 1991-92 and the Dhyan Chand Award for lifetime achievement in 2002.
questions.s: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

questions.q: The 2032 Summer Olympic Games will be hosted by
questions.e: The IOC awarded the 2032 Games to Brisbane, following Paris 2024 and Los Angeles 2028. India has expressed interest in a later edition, but has not been awarded the 2032 Games.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Census 2027:
1. Census is a subject in the Union List.
2. It is the first digital census, allowing self-enumeration by citizens.
3. The reference date of 1 March 2027 applies to the whole country, including snow-bound areas.
4. It is being conducted under the Census Act, 1948.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: For Ladakh and the snow-bound parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, the reference date is 1 October 2026; for the rest of the country it is 1 March 2027. It also includes caste enumeration.
questions.h: 1 March 2027 for the plains, 1 October 2026 for the snow.

questions.q: Which site was inscribed in July 2026 as India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.e: Sarnath was inscribed at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan on criteria (iii) and (vi). Bodh Gaya (2002), Sanchi (1989) and Nalanda (2016) were already on the list.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list:
1. Deepavali was inscribed in December 2025.
2. The 20th session of the Intergovernmental Committee was held at the Red Fort, New Delhi, the first time India hosted it.
3. Durga Puja in Kolkata was inscribed in 2021.
4. The Kumbh Mela was inscribed in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kumbh Mela was inscribed in 2017, and Garba of Gujarat in 2023. Yoga was inscribed in 2016.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT founded or established in 1875?
questions.e: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867. Arya Samaj (Dayananda Saraswati), the Theosophical Society (New York) and the Aligarh college (Sir Syed Ahmad Khan) all date from 1875, the year also of Birsa Munda's and Sardar Patel's births.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Vande Mataram':
1. It was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1875.
2. It appeared in the novel Anandamath (1882).
3. It was first sung at a session of the Indian National Congress in 1896 by Rabindranath Tagore.
4. It was adopted as the National Anthem by the Constituent Assembly.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Constituent Assembly adopted Jana Gana Mana as the National Anthem and gave the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram equal honour as the National Song, on 24 January 1950. 2025-26 marks 150 years of its composition.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Birsa Munda's Ulgulan (1899-1900) was directed against the loss of tribal land and the breakdown of the khuntkatti system.
Statement-II: Outsiders (dikus), such as moneylenders and landlords, took over tribal lands under colonial revenue and forest policies.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Under the colonial land settlement the Mundas' communal ownership (khuntkatti) was eroded as outsiders gained land through debt and rent. This land grab is what explains the uprising's aims.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Vallabhbhai Patel received the title 'Sardar' during the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.
Statement-II: The Bardoli Satyagraha was a no-tax campaign against an enhancement of land revenue.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but the campaign's cause (the revenue increase) does not by itself explain why Patel got the title; it was the women of Bardoli who gave him the name after his leadership of the movement.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Arrange the following battles in chronological order:
1. Battle of Khanwa
2. First Battle of Panipat
3. Battle of Ghaghra
4. Battle of Chanderi
questions.e: Babur's victories ran from Panipat (1526) over Ibrahim Lodi to Khanwa (1527) over Rana Sanga, Chanderi (1528) and Ghaghra (1529) over the Afghans. March 2027 marks 500 years since Khanwa.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gandhi-Irwin Pact:
1. It was signed on 5 March 1931.
2. Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference.
3. The Government agreed to release all political prisoners, including those convicted of violence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Government agreed to release only non-violent political prisoners and allowed salt-making for domestic use in coastal villages. Bhagat Singh's execution on 23 March 1931 strained the pact before the Karachi Congress.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Match List-I (Leader of 1857) with List-II (Centre of revolt):
A. Nana Sahib
B. Kunwar Singh
C. Begum Hazrat Mahal
D. Khan Bahadur Khan
1. Lucknow
2. Bareilly
3. Kanpur
4. Arrah
questions.e: Nana Sahib led the revolt at Kanpur and Kunwar Singh at Arrah in Bihar. Begum Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow and Khan Bahadur Khan at Bareilly.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Emergency of 1975:
1. It was proclaimed on 25 June 1975 on the ground of internal disturbance under Article 352.
2. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
3. The 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as a ground for Emergency.
4. The Government of India observes 26 June as Samvidhan Hatya Diwas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Government declared 25 June, the day the Emergency began, as Samvidhan Hatya Diwas in 2024. The 44th Amendment (1978) made the proclamation harder to misuse.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch Emergency Provisions; PIB, Jul 2024

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indus Waters Treaty:
1. It was signed at Karachi in 1960, with the World Bank also a signatory.
2. The three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, were allocated to Pakistan.
3. India may use the western rivers for non-consumptive uses such as run-of-the-river hydropower.
4. In April 2025, India announced that it was holding the treaty in abeyance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The treaty gives the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India and the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan, with limited Indian use of the latter. The second statement reverses the allocation.
questions.s: Ministry of Jal Shakti / PIB, Apr 2025

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 at the New Delhi Summit in 2023.
2. Indonesia became a full member of BRICS in January 2025.
3. Argentina joined BRICS as a full member in January 2024.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined BRICS in January 2024. Argentina was invited but declined after its change of government.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kakori conspiracy:
1. The Kakori train action took place on 9 August 1925.
2. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged in December 1927.
3. The Hindustan Republican Association was reorganised as the HSRA in 1928.
4. Chandrashekhar Azad was hanged for his role in the Kakori case.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Azad evaded arrest and died in a police encounter at Alfred Park, Allahabad, in 1931. The HRA was reorganised at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, in 1928.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about United Nations International Years:
1. 2026 has been designated as the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.
2. 2026 has been designated as the International Year of the Woman Farmer.
3. 2025 was the International Year of Millets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The International Year of Millets was 2023 and India led the proposal. The UN designated 2026 for rangelands and pastoralists, the woman farmer, and volunteers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Booker Prize 2025:
1. The winning book Heart Lamp is a collection of short stories originally written in Kannada.
2. It was translated into English by Deepa Bhasthi.
3. It was the first Indian work to win the International Booker Prize.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq won the 2025 prize. Geetanjali Shree's Hindi novel Tomb of Sand, translated by Daisy Rockwell, won in 2022, so Heart Lamp was not the first Indian winner.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India in space:
1. Shubhanshu Shukla travelled to the International Space Station on the Axiom-4 mission in June 2025.
2. He was the first Indian to visit the International Space Station.
3. Rakesh Sharma flew on the Soviet Soyuz T-11 mission in 1984.
4. SpaDeX made India the third country to demonstrate in-space docking.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India became the fourth country, after the United States, Russia and China, to dock spacecraft in orbit with SpaDeX in January 2025. Shukla was the second Indian in space after Rakesh Sharma.

questions.q: The UNFCCC COP31 in November 2026 is to be hosted by
o: the United Arab Emirates at Dubai
Australia at Sydney, with Türkiye leading the negotiations
Türkiye at Antalya, with Australia leading the negotiations
questions.e: Under a compromise reached at COP30, Türkiye hosts COP31 while Australia presides over the negotiations. Belém hosted COP30 in 2025 and Dubai COP28 in 2023.
questions.s: Australian PM office, Nov 2025; Climate Home News, Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vibhajan Vibhishika Smriti Diwas is observed on 14 August.
2. National Space Day on 23 August commemorates the launch of Aryabhata.
3. Samvidhan Divas is observed on 26 November.
4. Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is observed on 31 October.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: National Space Day marks the landing of Chandrayaan-3 on 23 August 2023, and Janjatiya Gaurav Divas falls on 15 November, Birsa Munda's birth anniversary. 31 October is Rashtriya Ekta Diwas.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:
1. Its first session was held on 9 December 1946.
2. Rajendra Prasad was elected its permanent President.
3. The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1946.
4. B. N. Rau chaired the Drafting Committee.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947 under B. R. Ambedkar; B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser. Sachchidananda Sinha was the provisional president of the first sitting.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch Making of the Constitution

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nobel Prizes for 2026:
1. The Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to Anne Carson of Canada.
2. The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, a former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.
3. Navi Pillay is a citizen of Sri Lanka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Navi Pillay is South African, of Indian origin, and a former judge and UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. Anne Carson was recognised for work that creates new forms while engaging with the classical tradition.
questions.s: Al Jazeera, 9 Oct 2026; Khaleej Times, Oct 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1917.
2. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919.
3. Michael O'Dwyer was assassinated in London by Udham Singh in 1940.
4. General Dyer was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rowlatt Act was passed in March 1919 after the Rowlatt Committee reported, and it triggered the Rowlatt Satyagraha. Sir Michael O'Dwyer, not Dyer, was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Revolt of 1857:
1. Mangal Pandey's act took place at Meerut on 29 March 1857.
2. The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
3. The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred the Company's rule to the British Crown.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mangal Pandey's act took place at Barrackpore, near Calcutta, on 29 March 1857, before the Meerut outbreak. The 1858 Act ended Company rule and created the office of Secretary of State for India.

questions.q: Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi on
questions.e: Gandhi began the march from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 5 April; he broke the salt law by picking up salt on 6 April. 8 August 1942 is the date of the Quit India resolution.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Match List-I (Slogan) with List-II (Person):
A. Do or Die
B. Inquilab Zindabad
C. Dilli Chalo
D. Swaraj is my birthright
1. Hasrat Mohani
2. Subhas Chandra Bose
3. Bal Gangadhar Tilak
4. Mahatma Gandhi
questions.e: Gandhi gave 'Do or Die' in 1942, Hasrat Mohani coined 'Inquilab Zindabad', Bose raised 'Dilli Chalo' for the INA and Tilak declared 'Swaraj is my birthright'.
